phrase: Good morning everyone. Thank you for being here today.
useCase: Opening a presentation with a professional greeting and acknowledging the audience
example: Good morning everyone. Thank you for being here today. I'm excited to share our team's progress on the sustainability initiative.
practicePrompt: You're about to deliver a quarterly update presentation. Open with a professional greeting using this phrase.

phrase: Today I'd like to walk you through...
useCase: Introducing the main topic or structure of the presentation
example: Today I'd like to walk you through our new onboarding process and show you how it reduces time-to-productivity by 30%.
practicePrompt: You're presenting a new process to the leadership team. Introduce your topic using this phrase.

phrase: As you can see on this slide...
useCase: Directing the audience's attention to a visual element in the presentation
example: As you can see on this slide, our customer satisfaction scores have increased steadily over the past three quarters.
practicePrompt: You're showing a chart during your presentation. Direct attention to it using this phrase.

phrase: This brings me to my next point.
useCase: Transitioning smoothly from one section of the presentation to the next
example: We've covered the market analysis. This brings me to my next point, which is our recommended go-to-market strategy.
practicePrompt: You've finished discussing one section and want to move to the next. Transition using this phrase.

phrase: To put this into perspective, let me share a quick example.
useCase: Using a real-world example to make data or concepts more tangible for the audience
example: To put this into perspective, let me share a quick example. One of our clients reduced their processing time by 40% after implementing this solution.
practicePrompt: You've presented statistics that might feel abstract. Make them concrete using this phrase.

phrase: I'd like to highlight three key takeaways from this analysis.
useCase: Signaling that you are about to present the most important conclusions
example: I'd like to highlight three key takeaways from this analysis. First, revenue is up 12%. Second, customer churn has decreased. Third, our NPS score is at an all-time high.
practicePrompt: You've presented a detailed analysis and want to emphasize the main conclusions. Use this phrase.

phrase: Does anyone have any questions at this point?
useCase: Pausing during a presentation to check for audience understanding and invite questions
example: That's the end of the first section. Does anyone have any questions at this point before I move on?
practicePrompt: You've completed a dense section of your presentation. Check for understanding using this phrase.

phrase: In conclusion, I'd like to leave you with...
useCase: Beginning the closing section of a presentation with a final thought or call to action
example: In conclusion, I'd like to leave you with this thought: investing in employee development isn't just good for people, it's good for business.
practicePrompt: You're wrapping up your presentation. Deliver a strong closing using this phrase.

phrase: Let me now hand it over to my colleague who will discuss...
useCase: Transitioning the presentation to a co-presenter or panelist
example: That covers the technical overview. Let me now hand it over to my colleague Sarah, who will discuss the implementation timeline.
practicePrompt: You've finished your section of a joint presentation. Hand over to your co-presenter using this phrase.

phrase: Thank you for your attention. I'm happy to take any questions.
useCase: Closing a presentation and opening the floor for a formal Q&A session
example: Thank you for your attention. I'm happy to take any questions you might have about the proposal or the timeline.
practicePrompt: You've completed your presentation. Open the Q&A session using this phrase.
